entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Luke Belludi (c. 1206, Padua – 1286-02-17), known as Luke of Padua, was a pivotal Franciscan friar and theologian whose life anchored the nascent Franciscan order in northern Italy during the 13th century. As one of Saint Anthony of Padua's earliest and most trusted disciples, Luke became instrumental in solidifying Anthony's legacy and transforming local religious practice, establishing Padua as a significant spiritual center. His contributions extended beyond personal devotion, shaping the institutional development of the Friars Minor in a critical period of growth and theological definition.

Born in Padua around 1206, Luke joined the Franciscan order in 1221, a mere two years after its foundation by Saint Francis. He was a constant companion to Saint Anthony, present at his death in 1231, and subsequently became the driving force behind the construction of the monumental Basilica of Saint Anthony of Padua. Luke oversaw much of its initial phases and served as its first custos, effectively making him the guardian of Anthony's tomb and cult. Furthermore, he played a crucial role in the canonical process for Anthony's sainthood, providing essential testimony that led to Anthony's canonization in 1232, less than a year after his death. Luke also held the significant administrative post of provincial minister for the Franciscan province of Padua, guiding the order's expansion and theological integrity.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Luke of Padua's direct involvement in the construction of the Basilica of Saint Anthony and his role in Anthony's canonization transformed Padua into a major pilgrimage center, significantly amplifying the cult of Saint Anthony across Europe. His administrative leadership helped stabilize the Franciscan Order in Italy during its formative period, impacting its spiritual and institutional trajectory for centuries.
